title: Brazilian Morning Espetinho Skewers
summary: Start your day with a bold twist on a popular street food classic using this savory breakfast skewer inspired by Brazilian barbecue. Thick cubes of squeaky queijo coalho cheese are threaded onto skewers alongside juicy breakfast sausage links and sweet bell peppers. Grilled over high direct heat, the cheese forms a golden crispy exterior while staying soft inside, offering an incredible contrast of textures. A light brush of garlic oil marinade enhances the salty richness, while fresh chimney sauce adds a burst of herbal acidity. Served next to fried eggs, grilled plantains, and tropical fruits, this protein-packed meal delivers an invigorating morning energy boost. The combination of smoky char and savory herbs transforms simple breakfast staples into a memorable outdoor dining adventure. Perfect for weekend gatherings or sunny patio brunches, these vibrant skewers bring an authentic festival energy right to your early morning table.

steps.step: Submerge wooden skewers in cold water for thirty minutes to prevent them from burning on the grill.
Cut the firm queijo coalho cheese into one-inch uniform square cubes using a sharp chef knife.
Slice the pork sausage links into thick one-inch rounds matching the size of the cheese blocks.
Core the red bell peppers and cut them into broad square pieces suitable for threading onto skewers.
Peel the red onion and slice it into quartered wedges, then separate the individual thick layers.
Mince three cloves of fresh garlic finely on a board and place them inside a small mixing bowl.
Whisk olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper together to create a herb oil.
Thread a piece of sausage onto a soaked skewer followed by pepper, cheese, and onion pieces.
Repeat the threading pattern twice more until each skewer is filled tightly while leaving handle room.
Brush the prepared skewers thoroughly on all sides with the garlic herb oil using a silicone brush.
Arrange the seasoned skewers onto a large baking tray and let them sit at room temperature for ten minutes.
Finely chop fresh cilantro and flat-leaf parsley leaves together for the chimichurri dipping sauce.
Combine chopped herbs, red wine vinegar, chili flakes, and extra olive oil in a small bowl.
Set the chimichurri sauce aside at room temperature so all herbal flavors meld together nicely.
Preheat your outdoor charcoal grill or indoor cast iron grill pan over high direct heat setting.
Oil the grill grates lightly using paper towels dipped in vegetable oil held with long tongs.
Place the assembled skewers onto the hot grill grates, ensuring space between each for even heat flow.
Sear the skewers undisturbed for two minutes until dark grill marks form on the cheese and meat.
Turn the skewers ninety degrees using heatproof tongs to sear the second side for two more minutes.
Brush additional garlic herb marinade over the skewers while turning them constantly on the grill.
Monitor the cheese closely to ensure it turns golden and crispy without melting completely off skewers.
Continue grilling for a total of eight minutes until the sausage is cooked through and piping hot.
Transfer the charred skewers onto a warm serving platter lined with fresh foil to keep hot.
Squeeze fresh lime juice lightly over the hot skewers to add a vibrant pop of breakfast citrus.
Peel ripe plantains and cut them into half-inch diagonal slices for quick pan frying.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook plantain slices for three minutes per side.
Remove fried plantains when golden brown and dust them with a light pinch of sea salt.
Toast cassava flour in a dry pan for four minutes until lightly browned to make classic farofa.
Heat vegetable oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat to prepare fresh fried eggs.
Crack four eggs gently into the skillet without breaking the sunny orange egg yolks.
Fry eggs for three minutes until whites are set but yolks remain soft and deliciously runny.
Season the cooked eggs lightly with sea salt, ground black pepper, and sweet paprika powder.
Arrange two grilled skewers across each warm breakfast plate alongside two fried eggs.
Place sweet fried plantain slices neatly beside the skewers for extra morning energy.
Spoon toasted cassava flour farofa onto the side of each plate for classic Brazilian crunch.
Drizzle generous spoonfuls of fresh chimichurri sauce directly over the warm grilled cheese.
Garnish plates with fresh orange wedges to deliver a sweet tropical balance to savory meat.
Dust extra chopped cilantro leaves over the entire breakfast platter for bright color contrast.
Serve skewers immediately while cheese is warm, crispy, and pleasantly chewy inside.
Offer remaining chimichurri sauce in a small dipping bowl at the table for guests.
Pair with fresh tropical fruit juices like passion fruit or guava for a complete meal.
Enjoy this hearty Brazilian breakfast feast hot off the grill with family and friends.
